name: IM-2

surface_window.note: From landing (approximately 11:30 a.m. [CST] March 6, 2025) to end of mission (12:15 a.m. CST Friday [March 7, 2025]), as published.

outcome_note: Touched down at Mons Mouton at about 11:30 a.m. CST March 6, 2025, roughly 400 m from the intended site, and came to rest on its side in a 20 m crater. Because the lander was on its side, the PRIME-1 instruments could not accomplish their goals; NASA received some data before Intuitive Machines called an early end of mission at 12:15 a.m. CST March 7.

payloads.name: The Regolith and Ice Drill for Exploring New Terrain
payloads.purpose: Drill built to record temperatures and bring up samples from as deep as 1 m.

payloads.name: Mass Spectrometer for Observing Lunar Operations
payloads.purpose: Mass spectrometer analysing drilled material for subsurface volatiles.

payloads.name: Laser Retroreflector Array
payloads.purpose: Passive retroreflectors serving as a precise location marker.

sources.title: NASA Receives Some Data Before Intuitive Machines Ends Lunar Mission (RELEASE 25-025, Mar 07, 2025)

notes: The intended landing site was -84.78, 29.13 E (LROC 1401); the coordinate used is where Athena came to rest.
NASA counts three PRIME-1 payloads: the PRIME-1 page names TRIDENT and MSOLO, and the TO2-IM page lists PRIME-1 among the LRA's task orders.

site.name: Athena rest position, Mons Mouton
site.source_note: The coordinate where the lander came to rest, as published; used as given, not searched. Height and slope sampled from the 80 m LOLA model at the nearest post.

notes: Mission facts are compiled by hand from NASA pages, LROC images and the IAU Gazetteer; every record carries its sources, last read 2026-09-23.
1 of 1 missions have fields no source confirms; they are listed as unconfirmed, never filled in.
Numbers are Sun and Earth geometry at the target over the mission's surface window, not what any lander measured.
